shapes.mechanism: the last line of the adjacent structured-html component is a complete HTML OPENING-tag line (a multi-tag line such as a <table ...> or <ul ...> opening tag, i.e. the line contains more than the single complete tag); the pulldown-cmark 0.13.4 dialect opens a type-6 (HTML tag) block on it that runs to the first internal blank line, absorbing the following code component's fence line and its first code lines (those bytes stay structural/covered); the code lines AFTER the first internal blank line then parse as ordinary paragraph text and are exposed. The 139 B per document are the code lines' non-machine text; machine tokens inside the code (URLs, paths, inline code, identifiers, numbers) remain covered by the residual classes.
shapes.why_not_covered_by_released_R1: R1's ordered predicate is closing-tag-scoped (a closing-tag line immediately followed by a fenced/indented code component); a complete opening-tag line is not a closing-tag line, so R1 correctly did not fire (v3 R1 insertions = 0). The 008-g 51 B pool had produced the closing-tag variant (v2 shape); this fresh pool surfaced the opening-tag complement - a pre-008-h design fact (the dev corpus never composes it: 008-h dev regression 0), addressable at the builder/label-oracle level, not by a residual recognizer.
shapes.dialect_ground_truth: pulldown-cmark 0.13.4 HTML block starts (vendored source, firstpass.rs/scanners.rs): types 1-5 via the html-end-tag scan (<pre|style|script|textarea + EOL/ws/>; <!-- ... -->; <? ... ?>; <![CDATA[ ... ]]>; <! + ASCII alpha to first >); type 6 = < or </ followed by a name in the dialect's HTML_TAGS block-level list (case-insensitive) followed by EOL/space/tab/CRLF/>//>; type 7 = any complete single-line tag ending at EOL. Tag-based blocks (types 1-7) end at a blank line, so an unbarred opening-tag line directly above a fence absorbs the fence. Verified in pre-work against the pinned helper (sha256 5df9a11d...).

fix_specification.mechanism: extend the R1 composition predicate from closing-tag lines to ALL dialect HTML block-start lines (opening-tag lines included); on fire, insert the same exactly-one NEUTRAL-labeled blank-line barrier as the released closing-tag rule; builder asserts the invariant (a fenced or indented code component is never composed on the line following an HTML block-start line without a neutral barrier); the 008-g closing-tag behavior and the 008-h R1/R2/R3 contract otherwise stay intact
fix_specification.dev_edge_shape: (i) - structured-html block whose last line is a complete multi-tag opening line, immediately followed by a fenced code component with an internal blank line; barrier NEUTRAL/template-owned, fence + code body PROTECTED

shapes.implementation_constraint: the frozen 008-h test research/tests/test_008h_dialect_edge_protection.py::test_r1_not_on_non_closing_tag (byte-frozen; every test file is preserved) asserts 0 R1 insertions for a bare SINGLE complete opening tag line (<div>) immediately followed by a fence. The order's scope item 3(a) wording ('ALL HTML block-start lines') is therefore executed as the dialect-faithful block-start set MINUS that test-pinned corner (bare single complete type-6/7 tag at EOL), which the order's '008-h R1/R2/R3 contract otherwise stay intact' clause preserves; the interpretation is disclosed in REPORT-008I.md boundary_fidelity. Residual exposure of the pinned corner (if the pool ever composes it) is monitored by the pre-seal diagnostic and the as-is sealing rule.

shapes.byte_split_per_document: 18 + 10 + 2 (tag delimiter/name bytes of the unrecognized tag)
shapes.mechanism: a single-line multi-tag XML line: the tags with fully-ASCII names and attribute names parse as recognised inline HTML (structural, covered); exactly one tag carries a dialect-vocabulary name but a non-ASCII (Slovenian) ATTRIBUTE NAME. The dialect's inline-HTML rule recognises a tag as a whole only with ASCII attribute names, so that tag's bytes become candidate prose. The frozen xml-fragment residual class triggers on tag-NAME membership in the dialect vocabulary and therefore ABSTAINS (v2-parity guard: it abstains deliberately for non-vocabulary names, and this name IS vocabulary) - the tag delimiters/name bytes are exposed (18 + 10 + 2 B) while the interior machine tokens (an identifier, a number) are covered by their own classes.
shapes.dialect_ground_truth: inline-HTML attribute-name recognition (verified in pre-work against the pinned helper, sha256 5df9a11d...): attribute name first char must be ASCII alpha/_/:; remaining chars ASCII alnum/_.:-; a non-ASCII character ANYWHERE in an attribute-name position makes the whole tag unrecognised (its bytes = candidate prose); a non-ASCII character in an attribute VALUE (quoted or unquoted) does not affect recognition. Probes: <element ASCII-name="v"> recognised; <element ASCII-name=non-ascii-value> recognised; <element non-ASCII-attr="1"> NOT recognised; <element non-ASCII-attr> NOT recognised; </closing non-ASCII-attr="2"> NOT recognised.
shapes.why_not_covered: class-boundary behaviour of the frozen 008-g spec: the name-based trigger cannot see attribute-shape recognition failures. Pre-existing (byte-identical under the 008-g implementation per the pre-existence proof).

fix_specification.primary_branch: (a) bounded trigger refinement, EXTEND-IF-EVIDENCED: the xml-fragment class additionally fires when the tag name is in the dialect vocabulary but the tag as a whole fails inline recognition SOLELY because of a non-ASCII attribute name (one curated predicate, gated on the exact measured condition; vocabulary abstention preserved); committed iff (1) zero new safety exposures on the 3,000-document dev corpus + 008-g batch + 008-h dev-edge + new 008-i dev-edge and (2) the focused positive/negative tests pass

fix_specification.residual_grammar_growth: none beyond the predeclared single D1-5 trigger condition (primary branch only)

shapes.byte_split_per_document: 14 + 12 (TeX command names and the = operator in the TeX body)
shapes.mechanism: an adjacent malformed-incomplete-display-dollar component (an unterminated $$ opener followed by a prose line) is composed immediately before a complete display-dollar component. The dialect pairs the malformed opener with the COMPLETE component's opening $$ line (the DisplayMath event spans the two $$ lines and is structural), so the complete component's TeX body then parses as paragraph text. The frozen residual classes cover numbers, identifier runs, and brace groups but NOT TeX command names (\frac, \quad, \text) or the = operator (14 + 12 B). Dialect pairing plus frozen class-boundary behaviour (no TeX-command residual class exists in the 008-g spec; the TeX classes are paren/bracket/env only). Pre-existing (byte-identical under the 008-g implementation).
shapes.dialect_ground_truth: display-math pairing (pulldown-cmark 0.13.4, verified in pre-work against the pinned helper, sha256 5df9a11d...): a $$ line OPENS a DisplayMath block only if the next $$ line occurs before any blank line; if a blank line comes first, the $$ degrades to literal paragraph text (lazy continuation) and cannot pair across it. Consequence: exactly ONE NEUTRAL-labeled blank line between the malformed-incomplete-display-dollar component and a following display-dollar component breaks the cross-pairing (verified: with the barrier the first $$ is plain text and the complete component is a proper DisplayMath; without it, the cross-paired DisplayMath spans the two opener lines and the TeX body is exposed). The predeclared one-NEUTRAL-blank-line barrier therefore WORKS and no substitution is needed.

fix_specification.mechanism: a malformed-incomplete-display-dollar component must not be composed immediately before a component whose first line is a $$ display-dollar opener; on fire, insert one NEUTRAL-labeled blank line (predeclared barrier; verified working in pre-work); NO new TeX-command residual class (paren/bracket/env only, 008-g spec)
fix_specification.dev_edge_shape: (iii) - malformed-incomplete-display-dollar (unterminated $$ + prose line), one NEUTRAL blank-line barrier, then a complete $$...$$ display-dollar component; malformed $$ POLICY_EXPOSED (oracle-refined, malformed class), barrier NEUTRAL, complete component body PROTECTED
fix_specification.residual_grammar_growth: none (builder-level composition guard; no new class)
